title: A specialized readiness verdict bypasses canonical semantic validation

scenario.observed_change: A specialized machine-readable release-readiness path evaluates readiness-specific conditions but omits canonical semantic validation that enforces release-gate and proof-command invariants, allowing an input to satisfy the specialized checks while remaining semantically invalid.
controlled_inputs: product evidence that satisfies the specialized readiness-specific conditions
the canonical semantic validator and its release-gate and proof-command invariants
the specialized readiness action and its machine-readable acceptance result
mutable_state: the set of semantic validation failures considered before that readiness state is emitted
authority_boundaries: a specialized readiness projection or action versus the canonical semantic validator
a machine-readable acceptance verdict versus the underlying semantic acceptance invariants
operation_model: construct evidence whose readiness-specific records appear verified
make release-gate or proof-command linkage semantically invalid so the canonical validator rejects the same evidence
the specialized path omits the canonical checks and can report a ready result even though canonical validation fails

required_invariants.requirement: A reviewer must trace a specialized acceptance or readiness path into the canonical validation and downstream execution context needed to establish that it cannot bypass required semantic invariants.

must_investigate: the execution path taken by specialized readiness mode compared with the canonical semantic validation path
semantic invariants enforced by canonical validation but omitted from the specialized path
an adversarial input that the specialized path accepts while canonical validation rejects
must_identify: the specialized readiness path can emit an accepted or ready verdict for evidence that fails canonical semantic validation because required validation is bypassed
must_not_claim: that readiness-specific checks are sufficient without comparing the specialized path with the canonical semantic validator
a clean review based only on output-schema correctness or happy-path tests while the semantic-validation bypass remains reachable

provenance.note: The historical exact-head review found that the specialized release-readiness path could return ready while the canonical validator rejected the same evidence. This case isolates that semantic-validation bypass mechanism from other malformed-input findings in the same review.
